title: Written Claim Denials and Appeal Rights — NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
Tidemark denies a coverage on a claim under the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own) in writing, stating one denial reason:

| Denial reason | When it is stated |
|---|---|
| Not a flood event | the damage did not result from flood as defined |
| Loss during waiting period | the loss began before the coverage or increase took effect |
| No coverage on date of loss | the policy was lapsed, cancelled or nullified on the date of loss |
| Proof of loss not timely | under the proof-of-loss rule |
| Excluded property | the damaged items are not insured property (including basement contents beyond the listed basement items when basement contents are not covered) |
| Loss below deductible | the payable amount is zero after the deductible |

**Partial denials.** A partial denial covers only the denied coverage and does not stop payment of the others.

**Letter content.** The denial letter informs the insured that an appeal may be filed with FEMA within the tier's appeal window in calendar days of the denial date and that suit must be filed within the tier's suit limitation in calendar months of the denial date; Tidemark does not decide FEMA appeals.

**Illustration (hypothetical).** A claim where the contents are denied as excluded property while the building measures a loss above the deductible: the contents denial stands alone and the building coverage is still paid.
